title: SRD: a spell cast at a target it can't affect spends the slot and the caster perceives it did nothing; engine: Mage Armor on an armored creature is refused instead

problems: review: rejected (The fix gets the rule right. Mage Armor cast on an armored creature now spends the slot and does nothing. The caster sees a player-visible 'does nothing' event and the gm detail stays hidden. The tags cite clauses #8, #9 and #11. The unit test checks real behaviour: the slot count, the AC, the missing effect, and each event's visibility and rule. I'm rejecting it because both new events leave out ruling="R-15", although R-15 names this exact case (armor) and CLAUDE.md requires the tag. The fix also copies the hand-written invalid-target code from Hold Person instead of sharing one mechanism, so I filed that as a refactor follow-up.)

review: other dungdra/spells.py:1119 Wearing armor is exactly the case README ruling R-15 covers ('If a target fails a restriction such as creature type, wearing armor, or 0 HP, the spell is cast… a player-visible note that the spell did nothing'). The acceptance test this fix un-xfails is marked ruling="R-15". CLAUDE.md requires log events to carry ruling="R-nn" when a register ruling applies, but neither new event does: the player 'spell' event (rule=…targets#11) and the gm 'invalid_target' event (rule=…targets#8). Add ruling="R-15" to both and assert it in the unit test. Apart from that the behaviour is right: the slot is spent, nothing happens to the target, the caster gets a player-visible note, and the gm detail stays hidden. The clause tags are #8, #9 and #11, as they should be.
